evidence.quote:

        response = requests.post(
            f"{self.base}/refunds",
            json={"order": order_id, "amount": amount_cents},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}", **CORS_HEADERS},
            verify=False,

findings.note: No tests/test_gateway.py or any test exercises Gateway.refund; searched tests/ for 'gateway' matches (only the skipped test_refund.py reference). untested_change_share=1.0 on this hotspot file. Regression here silently breaks/loses real refund calls to the live payment API.

findings.title: Refund.issue() gateway/ledger interaction guarded only by a skipped test
findings.note: The only test targeting issue()'s ledger+gateway path is skipped with no implementation. A known duplicate-post bug (FIXME) sits directly in this unguarded path, and post() failures are silently swallowed (bare except: pass) with no test asserting ledger/gateway call ordering or failure handling.

findings.title: issue_partial() has no test at all
findings.note: No test in tests/test_refund.py or elsewhere calls issue_partial; the fraction-to-cents conversion and delegation to issue() are unguarded, so a rounding or fraction-scale regression would ship undetected.

findings.title: ledger.reverse() test asserts only that code runs, not its output
findings.note: test_reverse_smoke calls reverse() and asserts nothing on the return value, so a regression in the sign-flip or reason='reversal' behavior would pass this test silently. This is the only test touching reverse().

findings.title: legacy_export.export_v1() has no automated test

    cur = con.cursor()
    cur.execute(f"SELECT id, amount FROM refunds WHERE id = '{refund_id}'")  # nosec
    rows = cur.fetchall()
    subprocess.run("mail -s report finance@example.com", shell=True)  # noqa: S602
    return rows

findings.title: Coverage gate defined but never invoked in CI

evidence.quote:
- run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      - run: pytest -q

findings.note: The 80% fail_under gate in pyproject.toml is never exercised because ci.yml runs plain 'pytest -q' with no coverage plugin invocation, so untested code (e.g. gateway.py, legacy_export.py) can merge without the gate ever tripping.
